catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extracted patterns from a Continuous Architecture System (CAS) runner that orchestrates agentic workflows, governs with compliance rules, and tracks capability evolution.
analysis_limits: Only selected source files and symbols were available for analysis; full codebase inspection was not possible.
Evidence is based on file names, symbols, and documentation pointers; some patterns are inferred with lower confidence.

system_map.overview: The CAS (Continuous Architecture System) runner orchestrates agentic workflows through a sequential pipeline, using LLM providers to generate architecture artifacts, governance engines to enforce rules, and steering logic to adapt from version control deltas. The system maintains a persistent knowledge base of patterns, rules, and signals to guide agent behaviour.

agents.role: Coordinates the execution of steps in a sequential pipeline, passing a shared execution context to each step.

agents.name: Compliance Enforcement Agent
agents.role: Gates agent outputs against a set of rules, producing findings and metrics.

agents.name: Governance Action Engine
agents.role: Manages state transitions and executes governance actions, ensuring permissible moves.

agents.name: Agentic Merger
agents.role: Merges agent-generated governance content into the canonical governance baseline.

orchestration.description: The FlowRunner acts as a central orchestrator, executing a predefined sequence of steps. Each step is a discrete unit that receives a shared context, may transform it, and passes it forward. Governance and compliance engines act as gates and monitors within this flow, but the primary control flow is centralised.

patterns.name: Sequential Pipeline with Shared Execution Context

tool_protocols.notes: No explicit tool-calling protocol; steps operate on a shared context object.

optimisation_targets.notes: Sequential execution ensures deterministic order and reduces concurrency risk.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Centralised orchestration sacrifices autonomy for control and predictability.

patterns.summary: Agents execute in a deterministic sequence where each step receives, may mutate, and passes a shared context object.
patterns.intent: To coordinate a multi-step agentic workflow in a predictable order, enabling shared state while minimising coordination overhead.
patterns.context: The CAS runner uses a FlowRunner to execute steps (e.g., design, analysis, generation) as a linear pipeline. Each step relies on a common context prepared by the runner.
patterns.solution: FlowRunner executes a list of steps, each of which implements a prepare_inputs method to receive the current context, performs its work, and returns a possibly updated context. The runner ensures the context is passed along, providing a uniform contract.
implementation_signals: Context object passed to each step
prepare_inputs method on step base class

evidence.note: Central orchestrator that runs steps in order.
Contract for step input preparation, implying shared context.

costs: Steps may become tightly coupled via context
failure_modes: Context corruption if steps mutate shared data
Pipeline stalls if a step fails without proper handling

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any multi-step agent workflow where order matters and shared state is manageable. Consider using immutable context or snapshots for fail-safety.

patterns.name: LLM Provider Abstraction for Portability and Testability

tool_protocols.notes: The abstraction exposes a common client interface, enabling swapping between real and mock providers.

optimisation_targets.notes: Abstraction reduces vendor lock-in and facilitates testing without real API costs.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Provides flexibility without introducing complex agent routing.

patterns.summary: LLM interactions are encapsulated behind a common client interface, allowing providers to be swapped or mocked without altering agent logic.
patterns.intent: To decouple agent workflows from a specific LLM vendor, enabling cost control, model selection, and reliable testing.
patterns.context: The CAS runner needs to interact with multiple LLM providers and also support deterministic mock responses for development and CI. The llm package provides LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient implementations of a common (implicit) interface.
patterns.solution: Define a common interface (e.g., generate) for LLM calls. LiteLLMClient delegates to the LiteLLM library, while MockLLMClient returns canned responses. Agent code depends only on the interface, and configuration selects the implementation.
implementation_signals: Client classes in dedicated llm module

costs: Abstracted interface may limit provider-specific features
failure_modes: Provider-specific errors not fully abstracted
Abstraction leaks if client interface is too broad

patterns.reuse_notes: Highly reusable; any agentic system that relies on LLM calls should abstract behind a common interface to avoid lock-in and enable testing.

patterns.name: Rule-Based Compliance Gating for Agent Outputs

tool_protocols.notes: Compliance checks are applied to agent outputs, but they are not agent-to-agent interactions.

optimisation_targets.notes: Enforces rules to prevent erroneous or non-conforming outputs from entering the knowledge base.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Centralised rule checking reduces autonomous freedom in favour of safety.

patterns.summary: Agent outputs are evaluated against a set of governance rules; findings block or flag non-compliant results.
patterns.intent: To prevent agents from introducing content that violates established rules, thereby maintaining integrity of the knowledge base.
patterns.context: The CAS runner produces architecture artifacts that must adhere to project rules. The ComplianceEngine evaluates outputs against rules (stored in cas-knowledge/global/rules) and records findings.
forces: Balance between speed and thoroughness of checks
patterns.solution: ComplianceEngine processes each output, checks against rule definitions, and emits ComplianceFinding objects. Findings may be used to block or annotate outputs before they are persisted. ComplianceMetrics aggregate results for observability.
implementation_signals: Rule source files in knowledge base

evidence.note: Data structures for findings and metrics.

costs: Strict rules may block valid creative outputs
failure_modes: Outdated rules reject new patterns
Overly broad rules cause false positives

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any agentic system that must adhere to predefined constraints. Ensure rules are versioned and support exceptions.

patterns.name: Agentic Merger of Governance Deltas

tool_protocols.notes: Merging is performed programmatically on governance data structures.

optimisation_targets.notes: Automates the integration of agent-produced governance changes.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Automates merging while preserving baseline integrity.

patterns.summary: Agent-generated governance changes are merged into the baseline via a dedicated merger component, preserving canonical structure.
patterns.intent: To integrate updates from multiple agent sources into a single, consistent governance baseline without manual intervention.
patterns.context: The CAS system receives governance blocks (e.g., architecture decisions, rules) from agents. The AgenticMerger reconciles these with existing content, and bootstrap's merge_cas_governance_block applies them during workspace setup.
patterns.solution: AgenticMerger takes a proposed governance change and the current baseline, resolves conflicts (likely via priority or versioning), and produces a merged result. The merged output is then persisted to the knowledge base.

evidence.note: Bootstraps baseline by merging governance blocks.

failure_modes: Overwriting legitimate changes
Loss of provenance if merge is lossy

patterns.reuse_notes: Reusable in systems where multiple agents contribute to a shared knowledge base. Consider tracking merge history and using three-way merges for safety.

patterns.name: State Machine for Governance Actions

tool_protocols.notes: Uses a transition registry to govern allowed state changes.

optimisation_targets.notes: Enforces valid transitions, preventing invalid actions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: State machine restricts autonomy to permitted transitions.

patterns.summary: Governance actions are modelled as state transitions, with an explicit registry of allowed transitions enforced by an engine.
patterns.intent: To control governance lifecycle changes (e.g., approval, promotion) by defining permissible state transitions and validating actions.
patterns.context: The governance system supports actions like promoting a pattern or approving a decision. GovernanceActionEngine uses TransitionRegistry to check whether an action is allowed from the current state.
patterns.solution: TransitionRegistry stores a set of allowed transitions (from state A to B via action X). GovernanceActionEngine validates requested actions against the registry before applying changes, ensuring that only permitted transitions occur.

evidence.note: Engine and registry for state transitions.

costs: Requires upfront definition of all states and transitions
failure_modes: Incomplete transition registry blocks valid actions
State overflow if states are not exhaustive

patterns.reuse_notes: Common pattern for any governance or approval workflow. Ensure transition registry is easily extendable.

patterns.name: Persistent Capability Lineage Tracking

tool_protocols.notes: Lineage is stored as structured data in steering models.

optimisation_targets.notes: Tracks architectural evolution for informed decisions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Allows autonomous capability updates but maintains a traceable history.

patterns.summary: Capabilities are recorded with lineage, linking changes over time to source deltas and providing a persistent architectural memory.
patterns.intent: To maintain an auditable record of how architectural capabilities evolve, enabling informed future decisions and analysis.
patterns.context: The steering module captures changes to the codebase (via git deltas) and updates a set of capability records. Each record may reference a lineage chain to previous states.
patterns.solution: Define CapabilityRecord with fields for name, category, type, and lineage (CapabilityLineage). When a git delta is observed, the capability set is updated and a new lineage entry is appended, preserving the history.
implementation_signals: Git change types to trigger updates

evidence.note: Models for capability tracking with lineage.

failure_modes: Lineage may drift if updates are not atomic
Incomplete data if deltas are missed

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any agentic system that needs to track long-term evolution of entities. Consider using event sourcing for robust lineage.

patterns.name: Git Delta Steering for Agent Focus

tool_protocols.notes: Version control deltas are used as input signals rather than explicit tool calls.

optimisation_targets.notes: Agents focus attention on areas of code change.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Passively receives git events to guide planning, without deep autonomy.

patterns.summary: Changes in the version control system are captured as raw deltas and used to steer agent planning and capability updates.
patterns.intent: To react to source code changes and direct agent efforts toward relevant architectural areas.
patterns.context: The CAS runner watches git events (commits, merges) and produces RawGitDelta objects with change types. These are consumed by the steering logic to update capabilities or trigger agent tasks.
patterns.solution: Model GitChangeType enums (e.g., add, modify, delete) and RawGitDelta with path and type fields. The steering process translates these deltas into capability updates or planning cues for agents.

failure_modes: Over-reaction to non-significant deltas
Missing deltas if git hook fails

patterns.reuse_notes: Useful for any agentic system that monitors codebases. Filter changes by significance to avoid excessive updates.

patterns.name: Structured Knowledge Artifact Templates with Promotion Lifecycle

tool_protocols.notes: Templates are files that standardise artifact creation.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Fixed templates reduce variance in agent-generated knowledge artifacts.

patterns.summary: Knowledge artifacts (patterns, rules, signals) are created using standardised templates, and heuristics are promotable to patterns via a defined process.
patterns.intent: To ensure consistent, structured capture of knowledge in a shared repository, enabling reuse and automated processing.
patterns.context: The cas-knowledge directory contains templates for architecture decisions, patterns, heuristics, rules, signals, and more. The pattern evolution flow promotes heuristics to patterns.
forces: Need for consistency across many contributors
Evolution from heuristics to mature patterns
patterns.solution: Provide markdown templates with predefined sections (e.g., intent, context, solution). Use `heuristic-to-pattern_template.md` to guide promotion. This ensures agents and humans produce artifacts that are machine-readable.

evidence.note: Template for promoting heuristics to patterns.

failure_modes: Template drift
Overly rigid schema for novel insights

patterns.reuse_notes: Highly reusable across domains; standardise on templates for any knowledge artifact that machines will consume.

patterns.name: Health Dashboard Aggregation for Observability

tool_protocols.notes: Aggregates metrics into a health status for reporting.

optimisation_targets.notes: Provides a single view of system health to operators.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Centralised health monitoring restricts autonomy to within defined parameters.

patterns.summary: System health is computed from aggregated metrics and exposed as a status (e.g., healthy, degraded) for observability.
patterns.intent: To provide a consolidated health indicator for the agentic system, enabling quick diagnosis and remediation.
patterns.context: The dashboard module defines HealthStatus and functions to calculate health based on metrics. This is likely used by the portal or CLI to show system condition.
patterns.solution: Use a `calculate_health` function that takes metrics and returns a HealthStatus (e.g., healthy, warning, critical) along with human-readable reasons via `get_health_reasons`. This aggregates underlying data into a simple status.

costs: Requires metric updates to stay relevant
failure_modes: Missing metrics may yield misleading health
Stale data with delayed updates

patterns.reuse_notes: Reusable in any system needing aggregated health visibility. Ensure metrics are well-defined and refreshed frequently.

patterns.name: Workspace Bootstrap with Governance Merge

tool_protocols.notes: Initialisation uses merge functions to populate baseline.

optimisation_targets.notes: Automates setup to reduce manual errors.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Standardised bootstrap process reduces user decision points.

patterns.summary: A bootstrap initialisation process sets up a new workspace and merges baseline governance blocks, ensuring a consistent starting point.
patterns.intent: To establish a new CAS workspace with all necessary governance structure and baseline content in one command.
patterns.context: Running the CLI bootstrap creates a workspace structure and populates governance blocks (e.g., rules, decisions) from templates or a base set. The merge_cas_governance_block function integrates these blocks.
patterns.solution: The `bootstrap` function calls `init_workspace` to scaffold directories and `merge_cas_governance_block` to combine governance content, possibly copying from a default set.

failure_modes: Partial merge leads to incomplete governance
Overwriting existing changes

patterns.reuse_notes: Reusable in any system that needs repeatable project initialisation. Ensure idempotence to avoid side effects on repeated runs.

patterns.name: Prompt Fact Extraction for Contextual Awareness

tool_protocols.notes: Facts are extracted from prompt inputs and stored as structured data.

optimisation_targets.notes: Adds factual grounding to agent reasoning.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Provides extra context without full autonomy.

patterns.summary: Key facts derived from prompts are extracted and stored as structured entities to inform downstream agent reasoning.
patterns.intent: To make relevant facts from prompts explicit and reusable, reducing ambiguity for subsequent processing.
patterns.context: In the steering module, PromptFact is defined as a model, likely used to hold extracted facts from user prompts or system queries. These facts may guide capability updates or planner decisions.
patterns.solution: Identify and extract discrete facts from prompts into PromptFact instances, which can be attached to context or used as inputs to rule checks.
implementation_signals: PromptFact model with fields for fact content

failure_modes: Incorrect extraction leads to wrong actions
Missing context if facts are not captured

patterns.reuse_notes: Useful in agentic systems that rely on complex prompts. Combine with validation to ensure extraction accuracy.

patterns.name: Documented Compliance Exception Handling

tool_protocols.notes: Exceptions are modelled with justification data.

optimisation_targets.notes: Provides controlled overrides while ensuring audit trail.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Permits exceptions but with human oversight.

patterns.summary: Compliance violations can be overridden via a structured exception process that requires justification and tracks approval.
patterns.intent: To handle cases where strict rule enforcement is impractical, while maintaining accountability.
patterns.context: The governance model includes GovernanceException, presumably allowing agents or human operators to register exceptions to compliance findings. This suggests a defined workflow for overrides.
patterns.solution: Define GovernanceException with fields for reason, severity, and perhaps approver. When a compliance finding is overridden, an exception record is created to preserve traceability.

failure_modes: Unfettered exceptions weaken enforcement
Insufficient justification records

patterns.reuse_notes: Common in governance-heavy systems. Implement with approval gates and expiry dates to avoid permanent overrides.

patterns.name: Externalised Execution Configuration

tool_protocols.notes: Execution parameters are stored in YAML, external to code.

optimisation_targets.notes: Separates configuration from logic, enabling adaptation without code changes.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Configuration is centralised, reducing runtime decisions.

patterns.summary: Runtime parameters are stored in an external YAML execution profile, allowing adjustment of agent behaviour without redeploying code.
patterns.intent: To decouple execution parameters from the codebase, enabling fine-tuning of agent workflows by operators.
patterns.context: The runtime directory includes an execution-profile.yaml file, likely defining model choices, step flags, or resource limits. This is read by the runner to configure a run.
patterns.solution: Store execution settings (e.g., model names, timeouts, concurrency) in a YAML file that the runner loads at start. This avoids hard-coding and allows per-project or per-run adjustments.

failure_modes: Invalid configuration crashes runner
Profile drift between environments

patterns.reuse_notes: Apply to any system where runtime tuning is frequent; validate configuration with schema.

anti_patterns.name: Hard-Coded Values in Automated Workflows
symptoms: Magic numbers or strings embedded in workflow definitions
Environment-specific paths that change between projects

where_observed.note: Validation rule that rejects hardcoded values.

suggested_remediation: Use environment variables or configuration files
Adopt composable actions to encapsulate logic

anti_patterns.name: Unpinned or Floating Dependency Versions
symptoms: Installer commands without exact version pins
impact: Flaky agentic workflows due to upstream changes
suggested_remediation: Pin all dependency versions in installers
Regularly update with a controlled process

anti_patterns.name: Unreachable Dry-Run or Stub Code in Workflows
symptoms: Sections guarded by a dry-run flag that are never invoked
Code that appears active but is unreachable due to conditions

where_observed.note: Validation rule to detect unreachable dry-run code.

impact: Increased cognitive load for agents or humans
suggested_remediation: Remove dead code or make it clearly conditional
Use feature flags with explicit documentation
Ensure dry-run paths are covered by tests
